export const NAME_FORMAT_MESSAGE =
	"Use 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens. Start and end with a letter or digit.";

export function isValidNameFormat(name: string): boolean {
	return NAME_PATTERN.test(name) && !name.includes("--");
}

export function isReservedName(name: string): boolean {
	return RESERVED_NAMES.has(name);
}
import { DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, RateLimiter } from "@convex-dev/rate-limiter";
import { components } from "./_generated/api";

export const rateLimiter = new RateLimiter(components.rateLimiter, {
	providerRequest: {
		kind: "token bucket",
		rate: 2000,
		period: HOUR,
		capacity: 30,
	},
	providerCleanup: {
		kind: "token bucket",
		rate: 500,
		period: HOUR,
		capacity: 16,
	},
	nameAttempt: {
		kind: "token bucket",
		rate: 1000,
		period: HOUR,
		capacity: 200,
	},
	nameClaim: { kind: "token bucket", rate: 1000, period: DAY, capacity: 200 },
	memberLookup: {
		kind: "token bucket",
		rate: 200,
		period: HOUR,
		capacity: 50,
	},
	serverChange: {
		kind: "token bucket",
		rate: 1000,
		period: HOUR,
		capacity: 200,
	},
	userSync: { kind: "token bucket", rate: 10, period: HOUR, capacity: 3 },
});

export function tooManyAttemptsMessage(retryAfter: number) {
	const minutes = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(retryAfter / MINUTE));
	return `Too many attempts. Try again in ${minutes} ${minutes === 1 ? "minute" : "minutes"}.`;
}
# Decisions

Only choices that the code does not explain. Rewrite an entry when it changes; git keeps the history.

Node runs Next.js; Bun only installs, runs scripts, and tests. Next.js on Bun has open runtime issues.

The Content Security Policy is static in next.config.ts. Clerk's generated policy allows scripts from any host unless nonces make every page dynamic.

The header and the page fill the large viewport, so the footer is below the fold and every page scrolls. The scrollbar is then always present, and no `scrollbar-gutter` is reserved. A reserved gutter doubles the scrollbar padding that Clerk's modal adds when it locks scrolling, which moves the page sideways.

`/` is one page for everyone. Signed-in parts render in the browser inside fixed-size regions, so the page stays static. Each server gets its own protected page.

Clerk's prebuilt components do sign-in, sign-up, and the profile inside the app: `<SignIn />` on `/sign-in`, and `<UserButton />`, which opens `<UserProfile />`. They include CAPTCHA, legal consent, the username step after Google sign-up, and reverification, which custom flows must build and maintain. There is no sign-up URL, so `<SignIn />` signs up new users in the same flow and shows no sign-up link. Sign-in is email code or Google, sign-up is public, and usernames are required. Passkeys and MFA need a paid plan.

Clerk's components keep its default theme. `--clerk-*` CSS variables refer to the semantic tokens, and Clerk hard-codes round avatars, so element classes make them square. Clerk's primary color is the neutral primary, not the brand color, because Clerk also uses it for text links and selected items.

Clerk's component code loads from Clerk's CDN, not from the `@clerk/ui` package. The package pins that code but adds hundreds of dependencies, and clerk-js loads from the CDN anyway.

A username is the user's only handle and display name. Clerk stores usernames in lowercase and rejects duplicates that differ only in case.

Convex keeps a users table synced from Clerk, because users will see other users when servers are shared, and billing needs a local user. It is keyed by the Clerk user ID, not tokenIdentifier: the deployment trusts one issuer, and Clerk's webhooks and API know only that ID.

One function syncs a user from Clerk's current state. The Clerk webhook, the client, and hourly reconciliation call it because webhook delivery is not guaranteed. Incomplete profiles disable app access while retaining existing ownership. Confirmed account deletion removes the user and requests durable cleanup of owned infrastructure.

Server ownership is stored on the server, separate from membership permissions. Membership grants reads. Rename, power, member management, SSH management, and deletion have independent permissions; new memberships default to every permission the caller can grant. Delegates can grant only permissions they hold and cannot change or remove a member with broader permissions. Only the owner can transfer ownership, to an existing active member; the previous owner stays with every membership permission. The owner cannot leave; deleting the owner's account requests durable server deletion.

Platform permissions do not restrict direct SSH or filesystem access. Membership removal does not remove native SSH authorizations. SSH entries have no required platform-member association. Ownership transfer does not move the operator grant that funded an allocation; capacity stays reserved until that allocation's infrastructure is confirmed absent. Billing transfer is not implemented.

SSH files remain authoritative on the server. Explicit file updates compare observed bytes and metadata, coordinate cooperating writes, replace the file, and verify the result. This is not compare-and-swap against independent editors. An uncertain outcome must not trigger a blind retry or rollback. OpenSSH authentication and sessions retain their native behavior.

Server names are permanently claimed by one server identity. A server can rename back to its own historical name; other servers cannot claim it, even after deletion. Every claim stays in serverNames, and an old name resolves to the current one. The name follows DNS label rules because it may become a subdomain. The reserved list in convex/names.ts is deliberately large, and a reserved name is reported as taken.

The code and product copy use the same term, name. There is no separate display name.

Rate limits exist to protect the system, not to slow people down: an account may have one server or hundreds. Limits are per user; a global limit would let one attacker block everyone. Expected failures such as a taken name are returned instead of thrown, because a thrown error rolls back the rate limit attempt it counted.

Provider API pacing is separate from user admission. Cleanup has reserved worker capacity and API allowance. Operator grants authorize billable allocations before billing exists. Capacity is released only after owned provider resources are confirmed absent.

The server identity is independent of its allocation backend and provider name. Hetzner resources use an opaque controller identifier, allocation identifier, and resource kind for ownership checks. Human-readable infrastructure names contain no project or deployment name. New allocations resolve the current configuration; existing allocations retain theirs.

Convex function module paths do not accept hyphens, so Convex modules use snake_case with a directory-specific filename lint rule.

Server pages call `auth.protect()` themselves instead of matching routes in the proxy. Clerk deprecates `createRouteMatcher` in favor of checks at the resource.

All corners are sharp. The icon is a sharp square, so the site uses the same shape at every size. The Tailwind theme has no radius tokens.

Two typefaces give two voices. Chakra Petch (`font-display`) is for the logo, buttons, labels, and facts such as resource sizes: the places where the product acts or makes a promise. Onest (`font-sans`) is for everything people read, including headings. Chakra Petch alone feels distant to people who have never used a server, and Onest alone does not signal infrastructure. Chakra Petch is loaded at weight 500 only; Onest is variable, with body text at 350 and headings at 550.

Neutral colors are steps of Tailwind's stone palette, not custom values. Each semantic token maps to one step, dark mode uses the mirrored step, and each hover or active state is one step further toward the foreground. Brand states darken the brand color in both themes. Components use only semantic tokens, so a color changes in `globals.css` and nowhere else. The one value between steps is Clerk's dark card, halfway between the page and the surface. Clerk makes muted panels, and the items on them, successively closer to the foreground than the card. In dark mode the muted panels are the surface, and the card must be lighter than the page because shadows do not show. A full step from each would put the card on the surface too.

Every internal link, including the logo, uses one `Link` that fades on hover with the same transition as buttons. An animated underline needs an always-present transparent underline, and Chrome paints it in the selection color when the text is selected.

Components join class names with clsx, not tailwind-merge. A `className` prop adds classes and never overrides the component's own. tailwind-merge does not read the Tailwind theme, so it must be configured by hand for every custom token, and a wrong configuration silently deletes classes, for example `font-body` (a weight) next to `font-sans` (a family).

The theme follows the operating system's light or dark preference. There is no manual toggle, so the server needs no stored preference and the first paint is correct.

Research in docs/research is input, not instruction. `bun run research:import <share-url>` adds a conversation.

import {

	paginationResultValidator,
} from "convex/server";
import { ConvexError, type Infer, v } from "convex/values";
import { internal } from "./_generated/api";
import type { Id } from "./_generated/dataModel";
import {
	internalMutation,
	type MutationCtx,
	mutation,
	query,
} from "./_generated/server";

import {
	isReservedName,
	isValidNameFormat,
	NAME_FORMAT_MESSAGE,
} from "./names";
import {
	getMembership,
	memberAccess,
	requireServerAccess,
	requireServerOwner,
	requireUser,
} from "./server_access";

	deleteServer,

	allServerPermissions,
	includesPermissions,
	serverPermissions,
} from "./server_permissions";

const DELETE_BATCH_SIZE = 100;

const serverSummary = v.object({
	_id: v.id("servers"),
	name: v.string(),
	isOwner: v.boolean(),
	permissions: serverPermissions,
});

const memberSummary = v.object({
	_id: v.id("serverMembers"),
	userId: v.id("users"),
	username: v.string(),
	imageUrl: v.string(),
	isOwner: v.boolean(),
	permissions: serverPermissions,
});

// Expected failures are returned instead of thrown, so a rate limit attempt they consume is not rolled back.
const failure = v.object({
	ok: v.literal(false),
	field: v.union(v.string(), v.null()),
	message: v.string(),
});

type Failure = Infer<typeof failure>;

function fail(field: string | null, message: string): Failure {
	return { ok: false, field, message };
}

async function limitServerChange(ctx: MutationCtx, userId: Id<"users">) {
	const status = await rateLimiter.limit(ctx, "serverChange", { key: userId });
	if (!status.ok) {
		throw new ConvexError({
			message: tooManyAttemptsMessage(status.retryAfter),
		});
	}
}

// Checks a name for a new claim. Every check counts as an attempt, and only an available name counts as a claim.
async function checkName(
	ctx: MutationCtx,
	userId: Id<"users">,
	name: string,
	serverId?: Id<"servers">,
): Promise<Failure | null> {
	const attempt = await rateLimiter.limit(ctx, "nameAttempt", { key: userId });
	if (!attempt.ok) {
		return fail(null, tooManyAttemptsMessage(attempt.retryAfter));
	}
	if (!isValidNameFormat(name)) {
		return fail("name", NAME_FORMAT_MESSAGE);
	}
	const taken = await ctx.db
		.query("serverNames")
		.withIndex("by_name", (q) => q.eq("name", name))
		.unique();
	if (taken !== null && taken.serverId === serverId) return null;
	if (taken !== null || isReservedName(name)) {
		return fail("name", "This name is taken.");
	}
	const claim = await rateLimiter.limit(ctx, "nameClaim", { key: userId });
	if (!claim.ok) {
		return fail(null, tooManyAttemptsMessage(claim.retryAfter));
	}
	return null;
}

export const listMine = query({
	args: { paginationOpts: paginationOptsValidator },
	returns: paginationResultValidator(serverSummary),
	handler: async (ctx, { paginationOpts }) => {
		const user = await getCurrentUser(ctx);
		if (user === null) {
			return { page: [], isDone: true, continueCursor: "" };
		}
		const result = await ctx.db
			.query("serverMembers")
			.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id))
			.paginate(paginationOpts);
		const page: Infer<typeof serverSummary>[] = [];
		for (const membership of result.page) {
			const server = await ctx.db.get("servers", membership.serverId);
			if (server !== null) {
				page.push({
					_id: server._id,
					name: server.name,
					...memberAccess(server, membership),
				});
			}
		}
		return { ...result, page };
	},
});

// Returns null when the name is unknown or the user is not a member, so the response does not reveal which servers exist.
export const getByName = query({
	args: { name: v.string() },
	returns: v.union(serverSummary, v.null()),
	handler: async (ctx, { name }) => {
		const user = await getCurrentUser(ctx);
		if (user === null) {
			return null;
		}
		const nameRecord = await ctx.db
			.query("serverNames")
			.withIndex("by_name", (q) => q.eq("name", name))
			.unique();
		if (nameRecord === null) {
			return null;
		}
		const server = await ctx.db.get("servers", nameRecord.serverId);
		if (server === null) {
			return null;
		}
		const membership = await getMembership(ctx, server._id, user._id);
		if (membership === null) {
			return null;
		}
		return {
			_id: server._id,
			name: server.name,
			...memberAccess(server, membership),
		};
	},
});

export const listMembers = query({
	args: { serverId: v.id("servers"), paginationOpts: paginationOptsValidator },
	returns: paginationResultValidator(memberSummary),
	handler: async (ctx, { serverId, paginationOpts }) => {
		const { server } = await requireServerAccess(ctx, serverId);
		const result = await ctx.db
			.query("serverMembers")
			.withIndex("by_server_id_and_user_id", (q) => q.eq("serverId", serverId))
			.paginate(paginationOpts);
		const page: Infer<typeof memberSummary>[] = [];
		for (const membership of result.page) {
			const user = await ctx.db.get("users", membership.userId);
			if (user !== null) {
				page.push({
					_id: membership._id,
					userId: user._id,
					username: user.username,
					imageUrl: user.imageUrl,
					...memberAccess(server, membership),
				});
			}
		}
		return { ...result, page };
	},
});

export const create = mutation({
	args: { name: v.string(), requestId: v.string() },
	returns: v.union(
		v.object({ ok: v.literal(true), name: v.string() }),
		failure,
	),
	handler: async (ctx, { name, requestId }) => {
		const user = await requireUser(ctx);
		requestKey(requestId);
		const previous = await ctx.db
			.query("serverOperations")
			.withIndex("by_requester_id_and_request_id", (q) =>
				q.eq("requesterId", user._id).eq("requestId", requestId),
			)
			.unique();
		if (previous) {
			if (previous.kind !== "create")
				return fail(null, "This request ID was used for another command.");
			if (previous.name !== name)
				return fail(null, "This request ID was used for another name.");
			const server = await ctx.db.get("servers", previous.serverId);
			return server
				? { ok: true as const, name: server.name }
				: fail(null, "This server was deleted.");
		}
		const problem = await checkName(ctx, user._id, name);
		if (problem !== null) {
			return problem;
		}
		const reservation = await reserve(ctx, user._id);
		if (!reservation)
			return fail(
				null,
				"Server provisioning is not enabled or your server limit is reached.",
			);
		const serverId = await ctx.db.insert("servers", {
			name,
			ownerId: user._id,
		});
		await ctx.db.insert("serverNames", { name, serverId });
		await ctx.db.insert("serverMembers", {
			serverId,
			userId: user._id,
			permissions: allServerPermissions,
		});
		await provision(ctx, serverId, user._id, requestId, name, reservation);
		return { ok: true as const, name };
	},
});

export const rename = mutation({
	args: { serverId: v.id("servers"), name: v.string() },
	returns: v.union(
		v.object({ ok: v.literal(true), name: v.string() }),
		failure,
	),
	handler: async (ctx, { serverId, name }) => {
		const { user, server } = await requireServerAccess(ctx, serverId, "rename");
		if (server.name === name) {
			return { ok: true as const, name };
		}
		const problem = await checkName(ctx, user._id, name, serverId);
		if (problem !== null) {
			return problem;
		}
		const claim = await ctx.db
			.query("serverNames")
			.withIndex("by_name", (q) => q.eq("name", name))
			.unique();
		if (claim === null) await ctx.db.insert("serverNames", { name, serverId });
		await ctx.db.patch("servers", serverId, { name });
		return { ok: true as const, name };
	},
});

function requireDelegation(
	available: Infer<typeof serverPermissions>,
	requested: Infer<typeof serverPermissions>,
) {
	if (!includesPermissions(available, requested))
		throw new ConvexError({
			message: "You cannot change permissions outside your own access.",
		});
}

export const addMember = mutation({
	args: {
		serverId: v.id("servers"),
		username: v.string(),
		permissions: v.optional(serverPermissions),
	},
	returns: v.union(v.object({ ok: v.literal(true) }), failure),
	handler: async (ctx, { serverId, username, permissions }) => {
		const access = await requireServerAccess(ctx, serverId, "manageMembers");
		const granted = permissions ?? access.permissions;
		requireDelegation(access.permissions, granted);
		const lookup = await rateLimiter.limit(ctx, "memberLookup", {
			key: access.user._id,
		});
		if (!lookup.ok)
			return fail(null, tooManyAttemptsMessage(lookup.retryAfter));
		const user = await ctx.db
			.query("users")
			.withIndex("by_username", (q) =>
				q.eq("username", username.trim().toLowerCase()),
			)
			.unique();
		if (user === null) return fail("username", "No user has this username.");
		const status = await ctx.db
			.query("userAccess")
			.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id))
			.unique();
		if (status?.disabled)
			return fail("username", "This user cannot receive server access.");
		if (await getMembership(ctx, serverId, user._id))
			return fail("username", "This user is already a member.");
		await ctx.db.insert("serverMembers", {
			serverId,
			userId: user._id,
			permissions: granted,
		});
		return { ok: true as const };
	},
});

export const setMemberPermissions = mutation({
	args: { memberId: v.id("serverMembers"), permissions: serverPermissions },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { memberId, permissions }) => {
		const member = await ctx.db.get("serverMembers", memberId);
		if (!member)
			throw new ConvexError({ message: "This member no longer exists." });
		const access = await requireServerAccess(
			ctx,
			member.serverId,
			"manageMembers",
		);
		if (member.userId === access.server.ownerId)
			throw new ConvexError({
				message: "The owner always has every permission.",
			});
		requireDelegation(access.permissions, member.permissions);
		requireDelegation(access.permissions, permissions);
		await limitServerChange(ctx, access.user._id);
		await ctx.db.patch("serverMembers", memberId, { permissions });
		return null;
	},
});

// Leaving or removing a membership does not change native SSH authorizations.
export const removeMember = mutation({
	args: { memberId: v.id("serverMembers") },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { memberId }) => {
		const member = await ctx.db.get("serverMembers", memberId);
		if (!member) return null;
		const access = await requireServerAccess(ctx, member.serverId);
		if (member.userId === access.server.ownerId)
			throw new ConvexError({
				message: "Transfer ownership or delete the server before leaving.",
			});
		if (member.userId !== access.user._id) {
			if (!access.permissions.manageMembers)
				throw new ConvexError({
					message: "You do not have access to do this.",
				});
			requireDelegation(access.permissions, member.permissions);
		}
		await limitServerChange(ctx, access.user._id);
		await ctx.db.delete("serverMembers", memberId);
		return null;
	},
});

export const transferOwnership = mutation({
	args: { memberId: v.id("serverMembers") },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { memberId }) => {
		const member = await ctx.db.get("serverMembers", memberId);
		if (!member)
			throw new ConvexError({ message: "This member no longer exists." });
		const access = await requireServerOwner(ctx, member.serverId);
		if (member.userId === access.user._id) return null;
		const user = await ctx.db.get("users", member.userId);
		const status = await ctx.db
			.query("userAccess")
			.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", member.userId))
			.unique();
		if (!user || status?.disabled)
			throw new ConvexError({ message: "This user cannot receive ownership." });
		const allocation = await ctx.db
			.query("serverAllocations")
			.withIndex("by_server_id", (q) => q.eq("serverId", member.serverId))
			.unique();
		if (allocation?.deleteRequested)
			throw new ConvexError({
				message: "A server being deleted cannot change ownership.",
			});
		await limitServerChange(ctx, access.user._id);
		await ctx.db.patch("servers", member.serverId, { ownerId: member.userId });
		await ctx.db.patch("serverMembers", access.membership._id, {
			permissions: allServerPermissions,
		});
		await ctx.db.patch("serverMembers", memberId, {
			permissions: allServerPermissions,
		});
		return null;
	},
});

export const remove = mutation({
	args: { serverId: v.id("servers") },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { serverId }) => {
		const { user } = await requireServerAccess(ctx, serverId, "delete");
		await limitServerChange(ctx, user._id);
		await deleteServer(ctx, serverId, user._id);
		return null;
	},
});

export const deleteMembers = internalMutation({
	args: { serverId: v.id("servers") },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { serverId }) => {
		const members = await ctx.db
			.query("serverMembers")
			.withIndex("by_server_id_and_user_id", (q) => q.eq("serverId", serverId))
			.take(DELETE_BATCH_SIZE);
		for (const member of members) {
			await ctx.db.delete("serverMembers", member._id);
		}
		if (members.length === DELETE_BATCH_SIZE) {
			await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.servers.deleteMembers, {
				serverId,
			});
		}
		return null;
	},
});

// Runs after a user is deleted. A server whose owner is deleted is deleted too.
export const removeUserMemberships = internalMutation({
	args: { userId: v.id("users") },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { userId }) => {
		const memberships = await ctx.db
			.query("serverMembers")
			.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", userId))
			.take(DELETE_BATCH_SIZE);
		for (const membership of memberships) {
			await ctx.db.delete("serverMembers", membership._id);
			const server = await ctx.db.get("servers", membership.serverId);
			if (server?.ownerId === userId) await deleteServer(ctx, server._id);
		}
		if (memberships.length === DELETE_BATCH_SIZE) {
			await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.servers.removeUserMemberships, {
				userId,
			});
		}
		return null;
	},
});

import { ConvexError } from "convex/values";
import type { Doc, Id } from "./_generated/dataModel";
import type { QueryCtx } from "./_generated/server";
import {
	allServerPermissions,
	type ServerPermission,
} from "./server_permissions";
import { getCurrentUser } from "./users";

export async function requireUser(ctx: QueryCtx) {
	const user = await getCurrentUser(ctx);
	if (user === null) throw new ConvexError({ message: "Sign in to continue." });
	return user;
}

export async function getMembership(
	ctx: QueryCtx,
	serverId: Id<"servers">,
	userId: Id<"users">,
) {
	return await ctx.db
		.query("serverMembers")
		.withIndex("by_server_id_and_user_id", (q) =>
			q.eq("serverId", serverId).eq("userId", userId),
		)
		.unique();
}

export function memberAccess(
	server: Doc<"servers">,
	member: Doc<"serverMembers">,
) {
	const isOwner = server.ownerId === member.userId;
	return {
		isOwner,
		permissions: isOwner ? allServerPermissions : member.permissions,
	};
}

/** Membership grants reads; an explicit permission gates each platform change. */
export async function requireServerAccess(
	ctx: QueryCtx,
	serverId: Id<"servers">,
	permission?: ServerPermission,
) {
	const user = await requireUser(ctx);
	const server = await ctx.db.get("servers", serverId);
	const membership = await getMembership(ctx, serverId, user._id);
	if (!server || !membership)
		throw new ConvexError({
			message: "You do not have access to this server.",
		});
	const access = memberAccess(server, membership);
	if (permission && !access.permissions[permission])
		throw new ConvexError({ message: "You do not have access to do this." });
	return { user, server, membership, ...access };
}

export async function requireServerOwner(
	ctx: QueryCtx,
	serverId: Id<"servers">,
) {
	const access = await requireServerAccess(ctx, serverId);
	if (!access.isOwner)
		throw new ConvexError({
			message: "Only the owner can transfer ownership.",
		});
	return access;
}
import { type Infer, v } from "convex/values";

/** Platform authority only. These flags do not restrict direct SSH sessions. */
export const serverPermissions = v.object({
	rename: v.boolean(),
	power: v.boolean(),
	manageMembers: v.boolean(),
	manageSsh: v.boolean(),
	delete: v.boolean(),
});

export type ServerPermissions = Infer<typeof serverPermissions>;
export type ServerPermission = keyof ServerPermissions;

export const allServerPermissions: Readonly<ServerPermissions> = Object.freeze({
	rename: true,
	power: true,
	manageMembers: true,
	manageSsh: true,
	delete: true,
});

/** A delegate cannot grant or remove authority outside their own permissions. */
export function includesPermissions(
	available: Readonly<ServerPermissions>,
	requested: Readonly<ServerPermissions>,
) {
	return Object.entries(requested).every(
		([key, enabled]) => !enabled || available[key as ServerPermission],
	);
}

	serverAllocations: defineTable(allocationFields)

	serverMembers: defineTable({

import { verifyWebhook } from "@clerk/backend/webhooks";
import { httpRouter } from "convex/server";
import { internal } from "./_generated/api";
import { env, httpAction } from "./_generated/server";

const http = httpRouter();

http.route({
	path: "/webhooks/clerk",
	method: "POST",
	handler: httpAction(async (ctx, request) => {
		let event: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof verifyWebhook>>;
		try {
			event = await verifyWebhook(request, {
				signingSecret: env.CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET,
			});
		} catch {
			return new Response("Invalid webhook signature.", { status: 400 });
		}

		if (
			event.type === "user.created" ||
			event.type === "user.updated" ||
			event.type === "user.deleted"
		) {
			const clerkUserId = event.data.id;
			if (clerkUserId === undefined) {
				return new Response("The event has no user ID.", { status: 400 });
			}
			await ctx.runAction(internal.users.syncFromClerk, { clerkUserId });
		}

		return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
	}),
});

export default http;

import type { User } from "@clerk/backend";
import { createClerkClient } from "@clerk/backend";
import { isClerkAPIResponseError } from "@clerk/backend/errors";
import {
	paginationOptsValidator,
	paginationResultValidator,
} from "convex/server";
import { ConvexError, type Infer, v } from "convex/values";
import { internal } from "./_generated/api";
import {
	type ActionCtx,
	action,
	env,
	internalAction,
	internalMutation,
	internalQuery,
	type QueryCtx,
	query,
} from "./_generated/server";
import { rateLimiter, tooManyAttemptsMessage } from "./limits";
import schema, { userFields } from "./schema";

const CLERK_PAGE_SIZE = 100;

export async function getCurrentUser(ctx: QueryCtx) {
	const identity = await ctx.auth.getUserIdentity();
	if (identity === null) {
		return null;
	}
	const user = await ctx.db
		.query("users")
		.withIndex("by_clerk_user_id", (q) => q.eq("clerkUserId", identity.subject))
		.unique();
	if (!user) return null;
	const access = await ctx.db
		.query("userAccess")
		.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id))
		.unique();
	return access?.disabled ? null : user;
}

function clerkClient() {
	return createClerkClient({ secretKey: env.CLERK_SECRET_KEY });
}

// Returns null until the Clerk account has every field that sign-up requires.
function toUserFields(user: User): Infer<typeof userFields> | null {
	const email = user.primaryEmailAddress?.emailAddress;
	if (email === undefined || user.username === null) {
		return null;
	}
	return {
		clerkUserId: user.id,
		username: user.username,
		email,
		imageUrl: user.imageUrl,
	};
}

async function storeFromClerk(ctx: ActionCtx, users: User[]) {
	const complete: Infer<typeof userFields>[] = [];
	const incomplete: string[] = [];
	for (const user of users) {
		const fields = toUserFields(user);
		if (fields === null) {
			incomplete.push(user.id);
		} else {
			complete.push(fields);
		}
	}
	if (complete.length > 0) {
		await ctx.runMutation(internal.users.store, { users: complete });
	}
	if (incomplete.length > 0) {
		await ctx.runMutation(internal.users.disable, { clerkUserIds: incomplete });
	}
}

// Reads the current state from Clerk, so the order in which events arrive does not matter.
async function syncUser(ctx: ActionCtx, clerkUserId: string) {
	let user: User;
	try {
		user = await clerkClient().users.getUser(clerkUserId);
	} catch (error) {
		if (isClerkAPIResponseError(error) && error.status === 404) {
			await ctx.runMutation(internal.users.remove, {
				clerkUserIds: [clerkUserId],
			});
			return;
		}
		throw error;
	}
	await storeFromClerk(ctx, [user]);
}

export const current = query({
	args: {},
	returns: v.union(schema.doc("users"), v.null()),
	handler: async (ctx) => await getCurrentUser(ctx),
});

export const syncCurrentUser = action({
	args: {},
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx) => {
		const identity = await ctx.auth.getUserIdentity();
		if (identity === null) {
			throw new ConvexError({ message: "Sign in to continue." });
		}
		const status = await rateLimiter.limit(ctx, "userSync", {
			key: identity.subject,
		});
		if (!status.ok) {
			throw new ConvexError({
				message: tooManyAttemptsMessage(status.retryAfter),
			});
		}
		const stored = await ctx.runQuery(internal.users.isStored, {
			clerkUserId: identity.subject,
		});
		if (!stored) {
			await syncUser(ctx, identity.subject);
		}
		return null;
	},
});

export const syncFromClerk = internalAction({
	args: { clerkUserId: v.string() },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { clerkUserId }) => {
		await syncUser(ctx, clerkUserId);
		return null;
	},
});

export const reconcile = internalAction({
	args: {},
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx) => {
		const clerk = clerkClient();

		for (let offset = 0; ; offset += CLERK_PAGE_SIZE) {
			const { data } = await clerk.users.getUserList({
				limit: CLERK_PAGE_SIZE,
				offset,
				orderBy: "+created_at",
			});
			await storeFromClerk(ctx, data);
			if (data.length < CLERK_PAGE_SIZE) {
				break;
			}
		}

		let cursor: string | null = null;
		for (;;) {
			const page: { page: string[]; isDone: boolean; continueCursor: string } =
				await ctx.runQuery(internal.users.listClerkUserIds, {
					paginationOpts: { numItems: CLERK_PAGE_SIZE, cursor },
				});
			if (page.page.length > 0) {
				const { data } = await clerk.users.getUserList({
					userId: page.page,
					limit: page.page.length,
				});
				const existing = new Set(data.map((user) => user.id));
				const missing = page.page.filter((id) => !existing.has(id));
				if (missing.length > 0) {
					await ctx.runMutation(internal.users.remove, {
						clerkUserIds: missing,
					});
				}
			}
			if (page.isDone) {
				break;
			}
			cursor = page.continueCursor;
		}
		return null;
	},
});

export const isStored = internalQuery({
	args: { clerkUserId: v.string() },
	returns: v.boolean(),
	handler: async (ctx, { clerkUserId }) => {
		const user = await ctx.db
			.query("users")
			.withIndex("by_clerk_user_id", (q) => q.eq("clerkUserId", clerkUserId))
			.unique();
		if (!user) return false;
		const access = await ctx.db
			.query("userAccess")
			.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id))
			.unique();
		return !access?.disabled;
	},
});

export const listClerkUserIds = internalQuery({
	args: { paginationOpts: paginationOptsValidator },
	returns: paginationResultValidator(v.string()),
	handler: async (ctx, { paginationOpts }) => {
		const result = await ctx.db.query("users").paginate(paginationOpts);
		return { ...result, page: result.page.map((user) => user.clerkUserId) };
	},
});

export const store = internalMutation({
	args: { users: v.array(userFields) },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { users }) => {
		for (const fields of users) {
			const existing = await ctx.db
				.query("users")
				.withIndex("by_clerk_user_id", (q) =>
					q.eq("clerkUserId", fields.clerkUserId),
				)
				.unique();
			if (existing === null) {
				await ctx.db.insert("users", fields);
			} else {
				await ctx.db.patch("users", existing._id, fields);
				const access = await ctx.db
					.query("userAccess")
					.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", existing._id))
					.unique();
				if (access) await ctx.db.delete("userAccess", access._id);
			}
		}
		return null;
	},
});

// Missing profile fields suspend application access without deleting owned infrastructure.
export const disable = internalMutation({
	args: { clerkUserIds: v.array(v.string()) },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { clerkUserIds }) => {
		for (const clerkUserId of clerkUserIds) {
			const user = await ctx.db
				.query("users")
				.withIndex("by_clerk_user_id", (q) => q.eq("clerkUserId", clerkUserId))
				.unique();
			if (!user) continue;
			const access = await ctx.db
				.query("userAccess")
				.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id))
				.unique();
			if (!access)
				await ctx.db.insert("userAccess", { userId: user._id, disabled: true });
		}
		return null;
	},
});

export const remove = internalMutation({
	args: { clerkUserIds: v.array(v.string()) },
	returns: v.null(),
	handler: async (ctx, { clerkUserIds }) => {
		for (const clerkUserId of clerkUserIds) {
			const existing = await ctx.db
				.query("users")
				.withIndex("by_clerk_user_id", (q) => q.eq("clerkUserId", clerkUserId))
				.unique();
			if (existing !== null) {
				const access = await ctx.db
					.query("userAccess")
					.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", existing._id))
					.unique();
				if (access) await ctx.db.delete("userAccess", access._id);
				await ctx.db.delete("users", existing._id);
				await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(
					0,
					internal.servers.removeUserMemberships,
					{ userId: existing._id },
				);
			}
		}
		return null;
	},
});

112				const existing = await ctx.db
113					.query("serverFindings")
114					.withIndex("by_controller_id_and_kind_and_provider_id", (q) =>
115						q
116							.eq("controllerId", scan.controllerId)
117							.eq("kind", scan.kind)
118							.eq("providerId", resource.id),
119					)
120					.unique();
121				if (reason) {
122					const fields = {
123						controllerId: scan.controllerId,
124						kind: scan.kind,
125						providerId: resource.id,
126						reason,
127						observedAt: Date.now(),
128						resolved: false,
129					};
130					if (existing)
131						await ctx.db.patch("serverFindings", existing._id, fields);
132					else await ctx.db.insert("serverFindings", fields);
133				} else if (existing)
134					await ctx.db.patch("serverFindings", existing._id, {
135						resolved: true,
136						observedAt: Date.now(),
137					});
138			}
139			const finished = args.nextPage === null && scan.kind === "primary_ips";
140			await ctx.db.patch("serverInventory", scan._id, {
141				page: args.nextPage ?? 1,
142				kind: args.nextPage
143					? scan.kind
144					: scan.kind === "servers"
145						? "primary_ips"
146						: "servers",
147				dueAt: Date.now() + (finished ? 300_000 : 10_000),
148				error: undefined,
149			});
150			return null;
151		},
152	});

154	import schema from "./schema";
155	export const run = internalAction({
156		args: { scan: schema.doc("serverInventory") },
157		returns: v.null(),
158		handler: async (ctx, { scan }) => {
159			let resources: { id: number; allocation: string; kind: string }[] = [];
160			let nextPage: number | null = null;
161			let error: string | null = null;
162			try {
163				await verifyController(Number(env.HCLOUD_FIREWALL_ID), scan.controllerId);
164				const response = await request(
165					`${scan.kind}?label_selector=controller-id%3D${encodeURIComponent(scan.controllerId)}&per_page=50&page=${scan.page}`,
166				);
167				resources = list(response?.[scan.kind]).map((value) => {
168					const row = object(value);
169					const labels = object(row.labels);
170					return {
171						id: idField(row.id),
172						allocation:
173							typeof labels["allocation-id"] === "string"
174								? labels["allocation-id"]
175								: "",
176						kind:
177							typeof labels["resource-kind"] === "string"
178								? labels["resource-kind"]
179								: "",
180					};
181				});
182				const next = object(object(response?.meta).pagination).next_page;
183				nextPage = next === null ? null : idField(next);
184			} catch (e) {
185				error = e instanceof ProviderError ? e.code : "inventory_failed";
186			}
187			await ctx.runMutation(internal.server_inventory.record, {
188				scanId: scan._id,
189				epoch: scan.epoch,
190				resources,
191				nextPage,
192				error,
193			});
194			return null;
195		},
196	});
197	import { Workpool } from "@convex-dev/workpool";
198	import { ConvexError, type Infer, v } from "convex/values";
199	import { components, internal } from "./_generated/api";
200	import type { Doc, Id } from "./_generated/dataModel";
201	import {
202		env,
203		internalMutation,
204		type MutationCtx,
205		mutation,
206		query,
207	} from "./_generated/server";
208	import { rateLimiter } from "./limits";
209	import schema from "./schema";
210	import { requireServerAccess } from "./server_access";
211	import { allocationStatus, resourceKind, resourceState } from "./server_model";
212	
213	const pool = new Workpool(components.workpool, {
214		maxParallelism: 2,
215		retryActionsByDefault: false,
216	});
217	const WATCHDOG_MS = 120_000;
218	const cleanupPool = new Workpool(components.serverCleanup, {
219		maxParallelism: 1,
220		retryActionsByDefault: false,
221	});
222	const IDLE_MS = 300_000;
223	const NEVER = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
224	
225	export function requestKey(value: string) {
226		if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{8,100}$/.test(value))
227			throw new ConvexError(
228				"Use a request ID with 8 to 100 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores.",
229			);
230	}
231	
232	export async function allocationFor(ctx: MutationCtx, serverId: Id<"servers">) {
233		return await ctx.db
234			.query("serverAllocations")
235			.withIndex("by_server_id", (q) => q.eq("serverId", serverId))
236			.unique();
237	}
238	
239	async function enqueue(ctx: MutationCtx, allocation: Doc<"serverAllocations">) {
240		await (allocation.deleteRequested ? cleanupPool : pool).enqueueAction(
241			ctx,
242			internal.server_worker.run,
243			{ allocationId: allocation._id, epoch: allocation.epoch },
244			{ retry: false },
245		);
246		await ctx.db.patch("serverAllocations", allocation._id, {
247			dueAt: Date.now() + WATCHDOG_MS,
248		});
249	}
250	
251	export async function reserve(ctx: MutationCtx, userId: Id<"users">) {
252		const grant = await ctx.db
253			.query("serverGrants")
254			.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", userId))
255			.unique();
256		if (!grant || grant.used >= grant.limit) return null;
257		if (
258			!env.HCLOUD_TOKEN ||
259			!env.HCLOUD_CONTROLLER_ID ||
260			!env.HCLOUD_LOCATIONS ||
261			!env.HCLOUD_FIREWALL_ID
262		)
263			return null;
264		const locations = env.HCLOUD_LOCATIONS.split(",").map((s) => s.trim());
265		if (
266			!locations.length ||
267			locations.length > 20 ||
268			locations.some((s) => !/^[a-z0-9]+$/.test(s)) ||
269			new Set(locations).size !== locations.length
270		)
271			throw new ConvexError("The server location configuration is invalid.");
272		const firewallId = Number(env.HCLOUD_FIREWALL_ID);
273		if (
274			!/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9]$/.test(
275				env.HCLOUD_CONTROLLER_ID,
276			)
277		)
278			throw new ConvexError("The controller identifier is invalid.");
279		if (!Number.isSafeInteger(firewallId) || firewallId <= 0)
280			throw new ConvexError("The server firewall configuration is invalid.");
281		await ctx.db.patch("serverGrants", grant._id, { used: grant.used + 1 });
282		return {
283			grantId: grant._id,
284			locations,
285			firewallId,
286			controllerId: env.HCLOUD_CONTROLLER_ID,
287			image: env.HCLOUD_IMAGE ?? "ubuntu-24.04",
288		};
289	}
290	
291	export async function provision(
292		ctx: MutationCtx,
293		serverId: Id<"servers">,
294		userId: Id<"users">,
295		requestId: string,
296		name: string,
297		reservation: NonNullable<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof reserve>>>,
298	) {
299		const operationId = await ctx.db.insert("serverOperations", {
300			serverId,
301			requesterId: userId,
302			requestId,
303			name,
304			kind: "create",
305			state: "pending",
306		});
307		const allocationId = await ctx.db.insert("serverAllocations", {
308			serverId,
309			...reservation,
310			backend: "hetznerCloud",
311			operationId,
312			resources: {
313				ipv4: { phase: "pending" },
314				ipv6: { phase: "pending" },
315				server: { phase: "pending" },
316			},
317			status: "allocating",
318			deleteRequested: false,
319			dueAt: Date.now(),
320			leaseUntil: 0,
321			epoch: 0,
322			failures: 0,
323		});
324		const allocation = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", allocationId);
325		if (allocation) await enqueue(ctx, allocation);
326	}
327	
328	export async function deleteServer(
329		ctx: MutationCtx,
330		serverId: Id<"servers">,
331		requesterId?: Id<"users">,
332	) {
333		const allocation = await allocationFor(ctx, serverId);
334		if (!allocation) {
335			if (await ctx.db.get("servers", serverId))
336				await ctx.db.delete("servers", serverId);
337			await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.servers.deleteMembers, {
338				serverId,
339			});
340			return;
341		}
342		if (allocation.deleteRequested) return;
343		const old = await ctx.db.get("serverOperations", allocation.operationId);
344		if (old && old.state !== "succeeded")
345			await ctx.db.patch("serverOperations", old._id, {
346				state: "superseded",
347				finishedAt: Date.now(),
348			});
349		const operationId = await ctx.db.insert("serverOperations", {
350			serverId,
351			...(requesterId ? { requesterId } : {}),
352			requestId: `delete_${allocation._id}`,
353			kind: "delete",
354			state: "pending",
355		});
356		// Preserve the worker epoch and resource identities: a create may still return.
357		await ctx.db.patch("serverAllocations", allocation._id, {
358			operationId,
359			deleteRequested: true,
360			status: "deleting",
361			error: undefined,
362			failures: 0,
363			dueAt: Math.max(Date.now(), allocation.leaseUntil),
364		});
365	}
366	
367	export const setGrant = internalMutation({
368		args: { userId: v.id("users"), limit: v.number() },
369		returns: v.null(),
370		handler: async (ctx, { userId, limit }) => {
371			if (!Number.isSafeInteger(limit) || limit < 0)
372				throw new ConvexError("The server limit must be a nonnegative integer.");
373			if (!(await ctx.db.get("users", userId)))
374				throw new ConvexError("The user does not exist.");
375			const grant = await ctx.db
376				.query("serverGrants")
377				.withIndex("by_user_id", (q) => q.eq("userId", userId))
378				.unique();
379			if (grant) await ctx.db.patch("serverGrants", grant._id, { limit });
380			else await ctx.db.insert("serverGrants", { userId, limit, used: 0 });
381			return null;
382		},
383	});

385	export const power = mutation({
386		args: {
387			serverId: v.id("servers"),
388			requestId: v.string(),
389			command: v.union(
390				v.literal("start"),
391				v.literal("stop"),
392				v.literal("forceStop"),
393			),
394		},
395		returns: v.id("serverOperations"),
396		handler: async (ctx, { serverId, requestId, command }) => {
397			const { user } = await requireServerAccess(ctx, serverId, "power");
398			requestKey(requestId);
399			const previous = await ctx.db
400				.query("serverOperations")
401				.withIndex("by_requester_id_and_request_id", (q) =>
402					q.eq("requesterId", user._id).eq("requestId", requestId),
403				)
404				.unique();
405			if (previous) {
406				if (previous.serverId !== serverId || previous.kind !== command)
407					throw new ConvexError("This request ID was used for another command.");
408				return previous._id;
409			}
410			const limit = await rateLimiter.limit(ctx, "serverChange", {
411				key: user._id,
412			});
413			if (!limit.ok)
414				throw new ConvexError("Too many server changes. Try again later.");
415			const allocation = await allocationFor(ctx, serverId);
416			if (
417				!allocation ||
418				allocation.deleteRequested ||
419				allocation.resources.server.phase !== "present"
420			)
421				throw new ConvexError("This server cannot accept a power command.");
422			const current = await ctx.db.get(
423				"serverOperations",
424				allocation.operationId,
425			);
426			if (current?.state === "pending")
427				throw new ConvexError("Wait for the current server command to finish.");
428			if (allocation.leaseUntil > Date.now() || allocation.action)
429				throw new ConvexError("The server is being checked. Try again shortly.");
430			const operationId = await ctx.db.insert("serverOperations", {
431				serverId,
432				requesterId: user._id,
433				requestId,
434				kind: command,
435				state: "pending",
436				deadlineAt: Date.now() + 300_000,
437			});
438			await ctx.db.patch("serverAllocations", allocation._id, {
439				operationId,
440				failures: 0,
441				error: undefined,
442				dueAt: Date.now(),
443			});
444			await enqueue(ctx, { ...allocation, operationId });
445			return operationId;
446		},
447	});
448	
449	export const status = query({
450		args: { serverId: v.id("servers") },
451		returns: v.union(
452			v.null(),
453			v.object({
454				status: allocationStatus,
455				error: v.union(v.string(), v.null()),
456				location: v.union(v.string(), v.null()),
457				ipv4: v.union(v.string(), v.null()),
458				ipv6: v.union(v.string(), v.null()),
459				observedAt: v.union(v.number(), v.null()),
460				operation: v.union(v.null(), schema.doc("serverOperations")),
461			}),
462		),
463		handler: async (ctx, { serverId }) => {
464			await requireServerAccess(ctx, serverId);
465			const a = await ctx.db
466				.query("serverAllocations")
467				.withIndex("by_server_id", (q) => q.eq("serverId", serverId))
468				.unique();
469			if (!a) return null;
470			return {
471				status: a.status,
472				error: a.error ?? null,
473				location: a.spec?.location ?? null,
474				ipv4: a.ipv4 ?? null,
475				ipv6: a.ipv6 ?? null,
476				observedAt: a.observedAt ?? null,
477				operation: await ctx.db.get("serverOperations", a.operationId),
478			};
479		},
480	});
481	
482	export const sweep = internalMutation({
483		args: {},
484		returns: v.null(),
485		handler: async (ctx) => {
486			const due: Doc<"serverAllocations">[] = [];
487			// Reserve half of each batch for cleanup, independently of new requests.
488			for (const deleting of [true, false])
489				due.push(
490					...(await ctx.db
491						.query("serverAllocations")
492						.withIndex("by_delete_requested_and_due_at", (q) =>
493							q.eq("deleteRequested", deleting).lte("dueAt", Date.now()),
494						)
495						.take(10)),
496				);
497			for (const allocation of due)
498				if (allocation.leaseUntil <= Date.now()) await enqueue(ctx, allocation);
499			return null;
500		},
501	});
502	
503	export const claim = internalMutation({
504		args: { allocationId: v.id("serverAllocations"), epoch: v.number() },
505		returns: v.union(
506			v.null(),
507			v.object({
508				allocation: schema.doc("serverAllocations"),
509				operation: schema.doc("serverOperations"),
510			}),
511		),
512		handler: async (ctx, { allocationId, epoch }) => {
513			const a = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", allocationId);
514			if (
515				!a ||
516				a.epoch !== epoch ||
517				a.leaseUntil > Date.now() ||
518				a.status === "deleted"
519			)
520				return null;
521			const pacing = await rateLimiter.limit(
522				ctx,
523				a.deleteRequested ? "providerCleanup" : "providerRequest",
524				{
525					count: 8,
526				},
527			);
528			if (!pacing.ok) {
529				await ctx.db.patch("serverAllocations", a._id, {
530					dueAt: Date.now() + pacing.retryAfter,
531				});
532				return null;
533			}
534			const patch = {
535				epoch: epoch + 1,
536				leaseUntil: Date.now() + WATCHDOG_MS,
537				dueAt: Date.now() + WATCHDOG_MS,
538			};
539			await ctx.db.patch("serverAllocations", a._id, patch);
540			const operation = await ctx.db.get("serverOperations", a.operationId);
541			if (!operation) throw new Error("Missing server operation.");
542			return { allocation: { ...a, ...patch }, operation };
543		},
544	});
545	
546	export const dispatch = internalMutation({
547		args: {
548			allocationId: v.id("serverAllocations"),
549			epoch: v.number(),
550			kind: resourceKind,
551		},
552		returns: v.boolean(),
553		handler: async (ctx, { allocationId, epoch, kind }) => {
554			const a = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", allocationId);
555			if (
556				!a ||
557				a.epoch !== epoch ||
558				a.deleteRequested ||
559				a.leaseUntil <= Date.now() ||
560				a.resources[kind].phase !== "pending"
561			)
562				return false;
563			await ctx.db.patch("serverAllocations", a._id, {
564				resources: { ...a.resources, [kind]: { phase: "uncertain" } },
565			});
566			return true;
567		},
568	});
569	
570	export const authorizePower = internalMutation({
571		args: {
572			allocationId: v.id("serverAllocations"),
573			epoch: v.number(),
574			operationId: v.id("serverOperations"),
575		},
576		returns: v.boolean(),
577		handler: async (ctx, args) => {
578			const a = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", args.allocationId);
579			return (
580				!!a &&
581				!a.deleteRequested &&
582				a.epoch === args.epoch &&
583				a.operationId === args.operationId &&
584				a.leaseUntil > Date.now()
585			);
586		},
587	});
588	
589	const update = v.object({
590		resource: v.optional(v.object({ kind: resourceKind, state: resourceState })),
591		spec: v.optional(
592			v.object({
593				location: v.string(),
594				imageId: v.number(),
595				serverType: v.string(),
596			}),
597		),
598		status: v.optional(allocationStatus),
599		ipv4: v.optional(v.string()),
600		ipv6: v.optional(v.string()),
601		actionId: v.optional(v.union(v.number(), v.null())),
602		clearAction: v.optional(v.boolean()),
603		error: v.optional(v.string()),
604		retry: v.optional(v.boolean()),
605		retryAfterMs: v.optional(v.number()),
606		complete: v.optional(v.boolean()),
607	});
608	
609	export const record = internalMutation({
610		args: { allocationId: v.id("serverAllocations"), epoch: v.number(), update },
611		returns: v.null(),
612		handler: async (ctx, { allocationId, epoch, update: u }) => {
613			const a = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", allocationId);
614			if (!a || a.epoch !== epoch) return null;
615			const patch: {
616				[K in keyof Doc<"serverAllocations">]?: undefined extends Doc<"serverAllocations">[K]
617					? Doc<"serverAllocations">[K] | undefined
618					: Doc<"serverAllocations">[K];
619			} = {
620				leaseUntil: 0,
621				dueAt: Date.now() + 5_000,
622			};
623			if (u.status && ["running", "off", "missing", "deleted"].includes(u.status))
624				patch.observedAt = Date.now();
625			if (u.resource)
626				patch.resources = { ...a.resources, [u.resource.kind]: u.resource.state };
627			if (
628				u.resource?.state.phase === "present" &&
629				a.resources[u.resource.kind].phase === "uncertain" &&
630				a.status === "blocked"
631			) {
632				patch.status = a.deleteRequested ? "deleting" : "allocating";
633				await ctx.db.patch("serverOperations", a.operationId, {
634					state: "pending",
635					error: undefined,
636				});
637			}
638			if (u.spec) patch.spec = u.spec;
639			if (u.ipv4) patch.ipv4 = u.ipv4;
640			if (u.ipv6) patch.ipv6 = u.ipv6;
641			if (u.clearAction) patch.action = undefined;
642			if (u.actionId) patch.action = { id: u.actionId, startedAt: Date.now() };
643			if (u.status)
644				patch.status =
645					a.deleteRequested && u.status !== "deleted" ? "deleting" : u.status;
646			if (u.error) {
647				patch.error = u.error;
648				patch.failures = a.failures + 1;
649				patch.dueAt =
650					Date.now() +
651					Math.min(3_600_000, 10_000 * 2 ** Math.min(a.failures, 8)) +
652					Math.floor(Math.random() * 5_000);
653				patch.dueAt = Math.max(patch.dueAt, Date.now() + (u.retryAfterMs ?? 0));
654				if (!u.retry || a.failures >= 8) {
655					patch.status = u.status === "missing" ? "missing" : "blocked";
656					patch.dueAt = Math.max(patch.dueAt, Date.now() + 3_600_000);
657					const operation = await ctx.db.get("serverOperations", a.operationId);
658					if (operation && operation.state !== "succeeded")
659						await ctx.db.patch("serverOperations", a.operationId, {
660							state: "blocked",
661							error: u.error,
662						});
663				}
664			} else {
665				patch.error = undefined;
666				patch.failures = 0;
667			}
668			if (u.complete && (!a.deleteRequested || u.status === "deleted")) {
669				const operation = await ctx.db.get("serverOperations", a.operationId);
670				if (operation?.state !== "succeeded")
671					await ctx.db.patch("serverOperations", a.operationId, {
672						state: "succeeded",
673						finishedAt: Date.now(),
674						error: undefined,
675					});
676				patch.dueAt = Date.now() + IDLE_MS;
677			}
678			if (u.status === "deleted") {
679				if (
680					Object.values(patch.resources ?? a.resources).some(
681						(r) => r.phase !== "absent",
682					)
683				)
684					throw new Error(
685						"Cannot release an allocation before resource cleanup.",
686					);
687				const grant = await ctx.db.get("serverGrants", a.grantId);
688				if (grant && a.status !== "deleted")
689					await ctx.db.patch("serverGrants", grant._id, {
690						used: Math.max(0, grant.used - 1),
691					});
692				patch.dueAt = NEVER;
693				patch.ipv4 = undefined;
694				patch.ipv6 = undefined;
695				if (await ctx.db.get("servers", a.serverId))
696					await ctx.db.delete("servers", a.serverId);
697				await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.servers.deleteMembers, {
698					serverId: a.serverId,
699				});
700			}
701			await ctx.db.patch("serverAllocations", a._id, patch);
702			return null;
703		},
704	});
705	
706	// Operator recovery requires explicit confirmation that an uncertain create never took effect.
707	export const retry = internalMutation({
708		args: {
709			allocationId: v.id("serverAllocations"),
710			confirmedAbsent: v.optional(resourceKind),
711		},
712		returns: v.null(),
713		handler: async (ctx, { allocationId, confirmedAbsent }) => {
714			const a = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", allocationId);
715			if (!a || a.status === "deleted" || a.leaseUntil > Date.now())
716				throw new ConvexError("The allocation cannot be retried now.");
717			const resources = { ...a.resources };
718			if (confirmedAbsent) {
719				if (resources[confirmedAbsent].phase !== "uncertain")
720					throw new ConvexError(
721						"Only an uncertain resource needs absence confirmation.",
722					);

import { v } from "convex/values";
import { internalMutation, internalQuery } from "../_generated/server";
import schema from "../schema";

export const get = internalQuery({
	args: { allocationId: v.id("serverAllocations") },
	returns: v.union(schema.doc("serverSshAccess"), v.null()),
	handler: async (ctx, { allocationId }) => await ctx.db.query("serverSshAccess")
		.withIndex("by_allocation_id", q => q.eq("allocationId", allocationId)).unique(),
});

export const prepare = internalMutation({
	args: schema.tables.serverSshAccess.validator.fields,
	returns: schema.doc("serverSshAccess"),
	handler: async (ctx, input) => {
		const allocation = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", input.allocationId);
		if (!allocation || allocation.deleteRequested || allocation.resources.server.phase !== "pending")
			throw new Error("ssh_bootstrap_not_pending");
		const existing = await ctx.db.query("serverSshAccess")
			.withIndex("by_allocation_id", q => q.eq("allocationId", input.allocationId)).unique();
		if (existing) return existing;
		const id = await ctx.db.insert("serverSshAccess", input);
		const stored = await ctx.db.get("serverSshAccess", id);
		if (!stored) throw new Error("ssh_bootstrap_missing");
		return stored;
	},
});

export const acceptHostKey = internalMutation({
	args: { allocationId: v.id("serverAllocations"), digest: v.string(), hostKey: v.string() },
	returns: v.boolean(),
	handler: async (ctx, { allocationId, digest, hostKey }) => {
		const allocation = await ctx.db.get("serverAllocations", allocationId);
		const access = await ctx.db.query("serverSshAccess")
			.withIndex("by_allocation_id", q => q.eq("allocationId", allocationId)).unique();
		if (!allocation || allocation.deleteRequested || !access ||
			access.bootstrapExpiresAt < Date.now() || access.bootstrapDigest !== digest ||
			allocation.resources.server.phase === "absent") return false;
		if (access.hostKey) return access.hostKey === hostKey;
		await ctx.db.patch("serverSshAccess", access._id, { hostKey });
		return true;
	},
});

==> convex/ssh/remove_keys.ts <==
"use node";

import { AuthorizedKeysFile } from "./authorized_keys";
import type { SshConnectionOptions } from "./connection";
import { SshError } from "./connection";
import type { SshFileObservation } from "./read_file";
import { writeSshFile } from "./write_file";

/**
 * Internal removal of occurrences from a caller's observation of this exact file.
 * The application must supply trusted connection/path data and authorize the user.
 * Removal does not require accepting a new key blob or option value. No key lookup
 * by fingerprint: duplicate occurrences retain their separate native meanings.
 */
export async function removeAuthorizedKeys(
	connection: SshConnectionOptions,
	path: string,
	observation: SshFileObservation,
	lines: readonly number[],
) {
	if (!lines.length || lines.length > 256)
		throw new SshError("invalid_request");
	// Copy all mutable request data before the first await.
	const expected = {
		...observation,
		bytes: Uint8Array.from(observation.bytes),
		attributes: { ...observation.attributes },
	};
	const edits = lines.map((line) => ({ kind: "remove" as const, line }));
	const file = new AuthorizedKeysFile(expected.bytes);
	const plan = file.plan(expected.bytes, edits);
	if (!plan.ok) throw new SshError("invalid_request");
	return writeSshFile(connection, path, expected, plan.candidate);
}
docs/decisions.md:31:Server names are permanently claimed by one server identity. A server can rename back to its own historical name; other servers cannot claim it, even after deletion. Every claim stays in serverNames, and an old name resolves to the current one. The name follows DNS label rules because it may become a subdomain. The reserved list in convex/names.ts is deliberately large, and a reserved name is reported as taken.
docs/decisions.md:35:Rate limits exist to protect the system, not to slow people down: an account may have one server or hundreds. Limits are per user; a global limit would let one attacker block everyone. Expected failures such as a taken name are returned instead of thrown, because a thrown error rolls back the rate limit attempt it counted.

## Assistant · 2026-09-14T10:50:25.738Z

I read all of `convex/` (except `_generated`), `decisions.md`, the backend plan, and the setup docs. I don't think we should keep the current shape. Right now we have two different ways of grouping files: `ssh/` uses a folder, and the server code uses a `server_` filename prefix. `names.ts` sits at the top level even though it only covers server names. And `limits.ts` (rate limits) is easy to confuse with the server grant `limit` ("your server limit is reached").

## Naming rules

Convex builds each function's path from its file path. Every rule below follows from that:

1. **The folder names the area; file names don't repeat it.** `ssh/` already does this. Server files move from `server_lifecycle.ts` to `servers/lifecycle.ts`, and SSH files don't get an `ssh_` prefix.
2. **Convex functions don't repeat their path.** You always call them through the path, so `api.servers.members.add` is right and `api.servers.members.addMember` repeats itself.
3. **Plain exports do carry the area name.** They're imported by bare name, so they have to make sense alone: `isReservedServerName`, `SshError`, `readSshFile`.
4. **A file is named after its main export**, minus the folder name.
5. **One definition per word.** Today "access" means three things: `userAccess` (account disabled), `server_access.ts` (permission checks), and `serverSshAccess` (a stored credential).
6. **Every table validator lives in `schema.ts`.** Today they're in three places: inline in `schema.ts`, in `server_model.ts`, and in `server_permissions.ts`. Other files can reuse them through `schema.tables.X.validator.fields`, the way `ssh/bootstrap_state.ts` already does.

## Proposed layout

```
convex/
  auth.config.ts convex.config.ts crons.ts http.ts schema.ts   ← Convex fixes these names
  rate_limits.ts            was limits.ts; used by both users and servers
  users/
    current.ts              get, sync, getCurrentUser, requireUser (moved from server_access)
    clerk.ts                sync, reconcile, isStored, listClerkUserIds, store, disable, remove
  servers/
    lifecycle.ts            create, remove, power, status (+ provision/deleteServer helpers)
    worker.ts               sweep, claim, dispatch, authorizePower, record, retry, run, WorkerUpdate
    grants.ts               reserve, set (was setGrant)
    inventory.ts            schedule, run, record
    hetzner.ts              provider client
    members.ts              list, listMine, add, setPermissions, remove, transferOwnership, removeAll, removeForUser
    names.ts                rename, resolve (was getByName), checkServerNameClaim, format/reserved checks
    reserved_names.ts       RESERVED_SERVER_NAMES (data only, ~1,400 lines)
    access.ts               requireServerAccess, requireServerOwner, getMembership, memberAccess, permission helpers
  ssh/
    authorized_keys.ts  connection.ts  read_file.ts  write_file.ts  write_file_script.ts
    remove_authorized_keys.ts   was remove_keys.ts (its export is removeAuthorizedKeys)
    inspect_public_key.ts       was inspect_key.ts (its export is inspectPublicKey)
```

## Names inside the files

- **`names.ts`:** `NAME_PATTERN`, `RESERVED_NAMES`, `NAME_FORMAT_MESSAGE`, `isValidNameFormat` and `isReservedName` become `SERVER_NAME_*`, `isValidServerName` and `isReservedServerName`.
- **Rate limit keys:** `nameAttempt`, `nameClaim` and `memberLookup` become `serverNameAttempt`, `serverNameClaim` and `serverMemberLookup`.
- **Tables:**
  - `serverInventory` holds scan cursors, so it becomes `serverInventoryScans`.
  - `serverFindings` becomes `serverInventoryFindings`.
  - `userAccess` gets a name that says "disabled".
- **Helpers:**
  - `requestKey` checks a request ID, so it becomes `requireRequestId`.
  - `allocationFor` becomes `getAllocation`, to match `getMembership`.
- **Problems I'd fix in the same pass** (CLAUDE.md requires it):
  - Single-letter locals `a` and `u` in lifecycle.
  - The same Workpool is created twice, once in `inventory` and once in `lifecycle`.
  - Magic numbers: `inventory` hard-codes `120_000` even though `WATCHDOG_MS` exists, and `300_000` is repeated in several places.
  - `power` writes its own rate-limit message instead of using `tooManyAttemptsMessage`.
- **Docs:** update the old paths in `decisions.md`, `server-backend-plan.md`, `setups/hetzner.md`, `crons.ts`, and the frontend's `api.users.*` calls.

## Risks

- **The other agent** is editing `schema.ts`, `convex.config.ts`, and the new `ssh/bootstrap_state.ts`. Its `serverSshAccess` table and `bootstrap_state` module fall under rule 5, and renaming files mid-edit would break its imports. I'd wait until it commits, then do the whole rename in one pass.
- **Live deployment data:** Convex can't rename a table. If the deployment has rows in the tables being renamed, the schema push fails until they're cleared (fine on dev) or migrated (needed on prod). Scheduled or queued jobs that point at old paths like `server_worker:run` would also fail, so the queue should be empty first. Resetting the renamed rate-limit counters is harmless.

Two things to confirm before I start:
1. Is there only dev data in these tables, or is anything in production?
2. Should I wait for the other agent to commit, or start now on everything except its three files?

Based on the search results, here's information about code organization in Convex, specifically regarding the "model" folder and helpers:

## Code Organization with the "model" Folder

Most of your code should live in a directory like convex/model, and your public API, which is defined with query, mutation, and action, should have very short functions that mostly just call into convex/model.

Most logic should be written as plain TypeScript functions, with the query, mutation, and action wrapper functions being a thin wrapper around one or more helper function. Organizing your code this way makes several of the refactors mentioned in this list easier to do.

## Helper Functions

Write helper functions in your convex/ directory and use them within your Convex functions. Helpers can be a powerful way to share business logic, authorization code, and more.

Helper functions allow sharing code while still executing the entire query or mutation in a single transaction. For actions, sharing code via helper functions instead of using ctx.runAction reduces function calls and resource usage.

This organizational pattern separates your business logic (in the `model` folder) from your public API endpoints, making your code more maintainable and reusable.

Based on the search results, here are the key best practices for Convex project structure and organizing functions:

## Function Organization

Best practices prescribe organizing functions by domain, using small composable mutations, and establishing clear query patterns for performance and caching. Specifically, functions should be organized by domain (users.ts, tasks.ts, etc.).

## Directory Structure

Most of your code should live in a directory like `convex/model`, and your public API, which is defined with query, mutation, and action, should have very short functions that mostly just call into `convex/model`. Convex uses file-based routing, so thoughtfully organize files with public query, mutation, or action functions within the `convex/` directory.

Functions can be registered within directories nested within the `convex/` folder. For example, a public function defined in `convex/messages/access.ts` has a function reference of `api.messages.access.h`.

## Additional Organization Tips

The recommended pattern for local components is to organize them in a `convex/components` folder, and you may want to structure functions so Node.js functions are in a separate directory to make them easier to spot.

These practices help maintain clean separation between your public API and internal logic, making code more maintainable and easier to refactor.

# Code Organization and Structure Guidelines

## Directory Layout

The documentation recommends organizing Convex code with a dedicated `convex/model` directory for shared logic:

> "Most of your code should live in a directory like `convex/model`, and your public API, which is defined with `query`, `mutation`, and `action`, should have very short functions"

This separates business logic from the public-facing API layer.

## Helper Functions Pattern

Helper functions should be plain TypeScript functions rather than wrapped Convex functions:

> "Most logic should be written as plain TypeScript functions, with the `query`, `mutation`, and `action` wrapper function being a thin wrapper"

Examples show helper modules like:
- `convex/model/users.ts` - contains `getCurrentUser()` function
- `convex/model/conversations.ts` - contains access control and data retrieval helpers
- `convex/model/scrape.ts` - contains single-page scraping logic

## API Organization

Public Convex functions live in files like `convex/conversations.ts` or `convex/teams.ts`, importing helpers from the model directory:

```
convex/
├── model/
│   ├── users.ts
│   ├── conversations.ts
│   └── scrape.ts
├── conversations.ts
├── teams.ts
└── crons.ts
```

The public API files are intentionally thin, delegating implementation to helper functions.

## Function Granularity

Use specialized functions over catch-all mutations:

> "Favoring more granular functions like `setTeamOwner` over `updateTeam` allows more granular checks"

This enables different access control logic per operation while maintaining code reusability through shared helpers.

# Code Organization Guidance from Convex Documentation

## File Structure

The documentation recommends organizing code within the `convex/` directory:

> "Write helper functions in your `convex/` directory and use them within your Convex functions."

## Module Organization

The examples show separating concerns into distinct files. For instance, helper functions for user operations are placed in `convex/userHelpers.js`, while team-related mutations live in `convex/teams.js`.

## Helper Functions

The guidance emphasizes helper placement for code reuse:

> "Helper functions allow sharing code while still executing the entire query or mutation in a single transaction."

This approach enables developers to consolidate business logic and authorization code without compromising transaction integrity.

## Generated Code

The documentation specifies that auto-generated files should be version-controlled:

> "Check this folder in to your git repo. That way your code will typecheck without needing to run..."

The `_generated/` directory contains schema-specific and function-specific type definitions customized to your application.

**Note:** The documentation provides no explicit recommendations regarding naming conventions for modules, functions, or overall directory hierarchy beyond the basic `convex/` folder organization.

# Query Names and File-Based Routing

According to the documentation, query naming follows a file-based routing system:

**Basic Structure:**
"The path and name of the file, as well as the way the function is exported from the file, determine the name the client will use to call it."

**Examples provided:**
- Functions exported from `convex/myFunctions.ts` are referred to as `api.myFunctions.functionName`
- Nested directories create hierarchical paths: a function in `convex/foo/myQueries.ts` becomes `api.foo.myQueries.listMessages`
- "Default exports receive the name `default`" and are called as `api.myFunctions.default`

**Non-JavaScript Clients:**
For other languages, string-based naming replaces the API object syntax: `"myFunctions:myQuery"` for `api.myFunctions.myQuery`, or nested as `"foo/myQueries:myQuery"`.

**Key restriction:**
The documentation states these naming conventions apply to queries, mutations, and actions, though HTTP actions use different routing mechanics. No explicit filename restrictions are mentioned in this section.

I found some useful information about organizing Convex codebases. Here's what the search results reveal:

## Organizing Large Convex Codebases

### Directory Structure and Best Practices

Most of your code should live in a directory like convex/model, and your public API, which is defined with query, mutation, and action, should have very short functions that mostly just call into convex/model.

The recommended pattern for local components is to organize them in a convex/components folder, but they can be stored anywhere in your project.

### Schema Organization

Create a schema.ts file inside the convex folder to create your schemas. Inside the convex folder is a _generated/ directory containing code customized to your convex functions.

### Code Organization Pattern

Most logic should be written as plain TypeScript functions, with the query, mutation, and action wrapper functions being a thin wrapper around one or more helper function.

### Performance Considerations for Large Codebases

TypeScript's type inference often slows down with large codebases. If you're running into language server performance issues, you can instruct the Convex CLI to generate static versions of the _generated/api.d.ts and _generated/dataModel.d.ts.

The search results emphasize separating concerns by keeping business logic in dedicated directories (like `convex/model`), organizing components in a `convex/components` folder, and using a central `schema.ts` file for database schema definitions.

## Assistant · 2026-09-14T10:56:24.654Z

I took "codex" to mean Convex.

## "One definition per word"

You're right, and I overstated it. The rule comes from ASD-STE100, which CLAUDE.md requires, but the same line says coding conventions win. In code, the file, folder, or table name already tells you which meaning a word has. `access` in `servers/access.ts` and in the `userAccess` table don't clash, so I'm dropping that rename.

The only real problem is two meanings side by side with nothing to tell them apart. There's one case of that today: `power` in `server_lifecycle.ts` calls `const limit = await rateLimiter.limit(...)`, and the same file checks `grant.limit`. That's the actual reason to rename `limits.ts` to `rate_limits.ts`.

## What the research shows

Convex gives very little official guidance on structure:
- **File paths become API paths.** `convex/foo/bar.ts` is called as `api.foo.bar.fn`, and folders can nest.
- **"Thin" public functions.** The docs suggest keeping queries and mutations short and putting most logic in plain helper functions in a folder like `convex/model/`. That's all it says about layout.
- **Nothing on naming** modules or functions.

Real projects don't agree with each other:

| Project | Layout | Function names |
|---|---|---|
| chef (Convex) | Flat, about 30 top-level files | — |
| ai-town | One folder per area; each folder has its own `schema.ts`, merged into the root schema | File names repeat the prefix inside the folder (`aiTown/agentDescription.ts`) |
| Convex agent component | Flat modules | Repeats the module name (`threads.getThread`, `messages.addMessages`) |
| Convex workpool component | Flat modules | Doesn't repeat it (`lib.enqueue`, `lib.status`) |

So there isn't one accepted "best" shape. What matters is picking rules we can apply the same way everywhere.

## Was my first proposal the best? No

- The "one word, one meaning" rule was too broad (see above).
- `listMine` didn't really belong in `members.ts`. It only landed there because I'd removed `servers.ts`.
- Splitting `users.ts` into a folder was symmetry for its own sake.
- Every folder-based layout has to answer "where do the functions for the server itself go?", and I dodged that by removing `servers.ts`.
- I missed that `server_model.ts` holds table validators, while Convex's docs use "model" for business logic.

## What `servers.ts` becomes: the options

| Shape | How calls read | Downside |
|---|---|---|
| **A. `servers.ts` next to `servers/`** | `api.servers.create`, `api.servers.members.add`, `api.servers.lifecycle.power` | The area lives in a file and a folder. A function can't share a name with a subfolder module. |
| B. Everything inside the folder | `api.servers.servers.create` | Repeats itself. Convex treats `index.ts` like any other file, so that doesn't help. |
| C. Split by job, no main file | `api.servers.names.rename`, `api.servers.members.listMine` | Some functions get forced into files where they don't fit. |
| D. Convex's `model/` pattern | `api.servers.create`, with logic in `model/servers.ts` | Every area gets two homes, and it's a logic refactor, not a rename. |

**My pick is A, with one rule:** `<area>.ts` holds the functions for that area's main table, and `<area>/` holds everything else.
- `users.ts` stays a single file.
- `ssh/` has no main table, so there's no `ssh.ts`.

The TypeScript types support a file and a folder with the same name, and the runtime paths (`servers:create` and `servers/members:add`) are different strings. I haven't pushed that to a dev deployment yet; I'd do that first.

```
convex/
  auth.config.ts convex.config.ts crons.ts http.ts schema.ts   (spreads ...serverTables)
  rate_limits.ts
  users.ts            current, syncCurrent, Clerk sync; requireUser moves here
  servers.ts          list, getByName, create, rename, remove
  servers/
    schema.ts         server tables and their validators (replaces server_model.ts)
    access.ts         access checks and permission helpers
    names.ts  reserved_names.ts
    members.ts        list, add, setPermissions, remove, transferOwnership, removeAll, removeForUser
    lifecycle.ts      power, status, provision and delete helpers
    grants.ts         reserve, set
    worker.ts         sweep, claim, dispatch, authorizePower, record, retry, run
    inventory.ts  hetzner.ts
  ssh/                unchanged
```

**Names inside files: qualify by distance.** A name that stays inside its folder doesn't repeat the area. For example, `isReservedName` inside `servers/` is clear. A name used from another area, or defined in a shared file, carries the qualifier: `SshError`, and `serverNameAttempt` in `rate_limits.ts`. This matches your point about context, and it keeps constants like `NAME_PATTERN` short.

## Decisions for you

1. **Where server functions live:** A, B, C, or D. I recommend A.
2. **Repeat the module name in function names?** (`members.add` or `members.addMember`.) I recommend not repeating it, because calls always include the path.
3. **Schema:** one root `schema.ts`, or a `schema.ts` per folder merged into the root (the ai-town approach). I recommend per folder for folders, and root for single-file areas like users.
4. **Table renames:** these are now free since there's no production data. For example, `serverInventory` holds scan cursors, so `serverInventoryScans` fits better.

## Timing

The other agent has now changed `server_lifecycle.ts`, `server_worker.ts`, `schema.ts`, and `http.ts`. It also added a top-level `convex/bootstrap_probe.ts` and `ssh/bootstrap.ts`. Moving files now would conflict with its work, so I'd do this in one pass after it commits. Want to settle the four decisions now?

Sources:

- [Convex Other Recommendations](https://docs.convex.dev/understanding/best-practices/other-recommendations)
- [Convex Query Functions (file-based routing)](https://docs.convex.dev/functions/query-functions)
